hints: Focus on what each test tells you about the functional group, Fehling's for aldehyde versus ketone and iodine for a specific methyl group.
Draw out the carbon skeleton for the two butanals, remembering C1 is the CHO carbon, and check which one has a CH3CH(OH) unit.
Now check chirality by looking for a carbon with four different groups, and keep only the aldehyde that passes both chemical tests.
walkthrough:
**Decode the Fehling's test**

Fehling's reagent is a gentle oxidising agent. It gives a brick-red precipitate only with aldehydes, not with ketones.

$$\text{R-CHO + Fehling's} \rightarrow \text{brick-red } \text{Cu}_2\text{O}$$

**Decode the alkaline iodine test**

Alkaline aqueous iodine is the iodoform test. It gives yellow $\text{CHI}_3$ with $\text{CH}_3\text{CO-}$ groups and also with $\text{CH}_3\text{CH(OH)-}$ groups, which are oxidised in situ to $\text{CH}_3\text{CO-}$.

**Draw the four candidates**

Write them with full skeletons. Number aldehydes from the CHO as C1, and ketones from the end nearest the C=O.

$$\text{B: CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{CH(OH)CHO}$$ 
$$\text{C: CH}_3\text{CH(OH)CH}_2\text{CHO}$$

**Apply all three clues**

Only 3-hydroxybutanal is an aldehyde (Fehling positive), contains $\text{CH}_3\text{CH(OH)-}$ (iodoform positive), and has C3 bonded to $\text{H, OH, CH}_3$ and $\text{CH}_2\text{CHO}$ (chiral centre). This fits all three observations perfectly.

options.A: 1-hydroxybutanone is $\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{COCH}_2\text{OH}$. It is a ketone so Fehling's is negative, and it has no carbon with four different groups so it is achiral. It fails two clues.
options.B: 2-hydroxybutanal is $\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{CH(OH)CHO}$. It is an aldehyde and chiral at C2, but the alcohol unit is $\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{CH(OH)-}$, not $\text{CH}_3\text{CH(OH)-}$. With no methyl directly on the CH(OH) carbon, the iodoform test is negative.
options.C: 3-hydroxybutanal is $\text{CH}_3\text{CH(OH)CH}_2\text{CHO}$. It is an aldehyde so Fehling's is positive, it contains $\text{CH}_3\text{CH(OH)-}$ so alkaline iodine is positive, and C3 is attached to four different groups so it is chiral.
options.D: 3-hydroxybutanone is $\text{CH}_3\text{COCH(OH)CH}_3$. It is chiral and gives a positive iodoform test due to $\text{CH}_3\text{CO-}$, but as a ketone it gives a negative result with Fehling's reagent.
